event_questions.label: E1
event_questions.not_this: A defect the claim itself attributes wholly to the tenant, or says he must remedy at his own expense, is no. A cause the claim calls shared or disputed is open, not no; a landlord's allegation that the tenant caused it, which the claim disputes, does not make this no.
event_questions.question: Does the claim state that the rented dwelling has a defect (for example mould, damp, or heating that fails) or that the tenant is disturbed in using the dwelling as agreed, without the claim itself saying that the tenant alone caused the defect or must remedy it at his own expense?

event_questions.label: E2
event_questions.not_this: A landlord's plan to raise the rent that has not been announced, demanded or charged; the initial rent agreed for a new lease; new accessory charges or reduced services without a higher rent.
event_questions.question: Does the claim state that the landlord has announced, demanded or charged a higher rent for the dwelling, by a notice, a letter, an invoice or otherwise (whether or not on an official form)?

questions.label: Q1
questions.not_this: A tenant who only contests the validity of the notice and does not ask for more time; a request for more time that the claim does not base on hardship.
questions.question: Does the tenant seek an extension of the lease because having to leave by the end date would be a hardship for the tenant or the tenant's family?

questions.label: Q2
questions.not_this: No: only a file stating that no notice of termination has been given at all (also a lease of limited duration that simply ends on its agreed date, a termination only announced or threatened, a notice given by the tenant). A notice the landlord says was sent and the tenant says never reached him is open, not no.
questions.question: Has the landlord given the tenant notice terminating the lease of the dwelling, and has it reached the tenant?

questions.label: Q3
questions.not_this: A tenant living with a partner who is neither spouse nor registered partner; spouses who do not use the dwelling as their family home.
questions.question: Does the claim state that the tenant is married or in a registered partnership and that the rented dwelling serves as the family home?

questions.label: Q4
questions.not_this: Claims the tenant asserted that the claim does not connect with the notice; a notice the claim attributes to another reason, such as the landlord's own use.
questions.question: Does the claim state that the landlord gave notice because the tenant had, in good faith, asserted claims under the lease (for example demanded repair of a defect or contested the rent)? The tenant's own account of the landlord's reason counts as stating it, also where the tenant gives it as a conviction or belief; it is open only where the claim itself says the reason is unknown, uncertain or one of several possibilities.

questions.label: Q5
questions.not_this: Arrears that the claim mentions while the notice is given for another reason (for example the landlord's own use); a dispute about a rent increase.
questions.question: Does the notice or the claim state that the landlord terminated because the tenant did not pay overdue rent or accessory charges within a time limit the landlord had set?

routing.question: Which tenancy dispute does the claim concern: a defect of the dwelling or a disturbance of its agreed use that the tenant did not cause (for example mould, damp, or heating that fails), a termination of the lease by the landlord, or a rent increase? A rent increase that the landlord accompanied with a notice of termination is a rent increase dispute: the rent-increase rules examine that notice (art. 269d para. 2 let. c).

text:
Guten Abend

Ich wohne seit März 2023 in einer Wohnung der Birkenrain Genossenschaft an der Schulhausstrasse 28 in Bern. Seit ein paar Wochen ist im Haus grosse Unruhe, und ich möchte vorbereitet sein.

Am 18. Mai 2026 war Herr Urs Morgan von der Genossenschaft bei uns im Treppenhaus und hat mit mehreren Mietern gesprochen. Er sagte, das Haus werde ab nächstem Jahr total saniert und es könne gut sein, dass die Genossenschaft allen kündigen müsse. Mit Geld hat das bei mir nichts zu tun. Ich bezahle meine CHF 1290 immer pünktlich, die Genossenschaft hat mir nie eine Frist zum Nachzahlen gesetzt, und Herr Morgan hat auch nichts in diese Richtung gesagt.

Wichtig: Gekündigt ist bis jetzt nichts. Ich habe weder einen Brief noch ein Einschreiben noch sonst etwas Schriftliches bekommen, es gibt nur dieses Gespräch im Treppenhaus. Meine Nachbarin Sabine Kuhn hat bei der Verwaltung nachgefragt, auch dort hiess es, Kündigungen seien noch keine verschickt worden.

Ich habe im April 2025 einmal wegen des tropfenden Wasserhahns in der Küche reklamiert, der dann auch repariert wurde. Ich glaube aber nicht, dass das irgendetwas damit zu tun hat. Herr Morgan hat ausschliesslich von der Sanierung gesprochen, und es betrifft ja das ganze Haus und nicht nur mich.

Meine Frage an Sie: Was kann ich jetzt schon tun, und worauf muss ich achten, falls tatsächlich eine Kündigung kommt? Ich möchte nicht im letzten Moment von einer Frist überrascht werden.

Mit freundlichen Grüssen
Seraina Bachmann
